name: OIBench
intro: OIBench 是面向强推理模型的高难度信息学奥赛基准，包含250道由资深竞赛教练原创且发布前未公开的中英文题目。每题配有难度标签、大规模测试与经执行验证的C++标准解，并以四种编程语言的全测试通过率及时间/空间完成曲线评估正确性和效率。
org: AGI-Eval, Beijing Normal University, Meituan, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
build_method: 专家原创命题, 人工复审, 可执行测试
metric: AC 通过率, 时间/空间完成曲线
task_type: 信息学奥赛, 竞赛编程, 代码效率
eval_feature: 原创抗污染, 四种编程语言, 全测试通过
scale: 250道原创双语题；含测试、难度标签与C++标准解
task_type_en: Olympiad in Informatics, competitive programming, code efficiency
build_method_en: Expert Original Problem Authoring, Human Review, Executable Tests
eval_feature_en: Original Anti-contamination Data, Four Programming Languages, All-tests-correct
intro_en: OIBench is a high-difficulty Olympiad-in-Informatics benchmark for strong reasoning models, containing 250 original Chinese and English problems authored by experienced contest coaches and kept private before release. Each problem includes difficulty tags, large official tests, and an execution-verified canonical C++ solution; evaluation measures all-tests-correct acceptance in four programming languages plus time/space completion curves.
scale_en: 250 original bilingual problems with tests, difficulty tags, and canonical C++ solutions

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2506.10481 Sections 3–5 and Appendices A.4 and A.9–A.10 plus the official AGI-Eval/OIBench release. The diagrams preserve problem sourcing from experienced ACM-ICPC/OI coaches’ private repositories or new authoring, strict unpublished-originality rules, Codeforces-style difficulty and competition-level tags, large and edge-focused official tests, canonical C++ solutions executed against all tests, six medal-level OI participants reviewing solvability/clarity/samples/TeX/Markdown, professional English translation using a coach-and-contestant terminology glossary, and search-engine verification that no problem was directly retrievable as of May 2025. The 250 bilingual problems are evaluated zero-shot in C++/Java/Python/JavaScript with the paper’s decoding exceptions, fixed Docker runtimes, all-tests-correct AC rate rather than pass@k, and separate time/space completion curves.
